title: CIA unclassified open-source intelligence system reportedly hit by cyberattack, Korean and Japanese outlets relay US media
date_note: US media reports are dated 24 November by the Kyodo and CBS Nocut articles (published 25 November); the date of the intrusion is not stated.
place: Washington, DC, United States (Kyodo dateline; location of the system not stated)
summary: CBS Nocut News says the AP reported a cyberattack on a CIA unclassified system used to analyse publicly available material, and that the ODNI said core functions and classified systems were not affected. Kyodo News, citing major US media, says no classified information was leaked. Nocut says the CIA did not immediately respond and the perpetrator is not identified.
plain: Korean and Japanese outlets relaying US media say a CIA system for open-source intelligence was hit by a cyberattack. They say classified systems were not affected, according to the ODNI as relayed by Nocut.
exec: A reported intrusion at a CIA unclassified system; per Nocut the ODNI says classified systems were unaffected, and the perpetrator is not identified.

validation.note: Both pages (CBS Nocut News, Kyodo via Kanaloco) relay the same US media reports; no English original, CIA or ODNI page was read. Status stays developing.
